<!-- maintheorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
There exists a divergence-free $u_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ whose
unique maximal smooth Euler solution has lifespan $T_*=T_*(u_0)$ with
\[
 0<T_*\le T<\infty,
\]
where $T$ is the accumulation time of the construction's target times.
Here the solution belongs to $C([0,S];H^m(\mathbb{R}^3))$ for every fixed
integer $m\ge0$ and every $S<T_*$. At its maximal time,
\[
 \limsup_{t\uparrow T_*}\|\nabla u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty,
 \qquad
 \int_0^{T_*}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\,dt=\infty.
\]
<!-- end maintheorem-1 -->
<!-- introlemma-1: body_md -->
\label{intro:lem:clock-child}
With the parameter choices of Subsection~\ref{intro:subsec:stage-parameters}, assume
$1/2\le a_j\le2$ and $\beta_jx_{j-1}^2\ge1/2$, as supplied by
\eqref{intro:eq:activation-ranges}.
For sufficiently large $J$ and then sufficiently large $x_{J-1}$,
\[
 \tau_j(S_j)\le\Theta_j,\qquad
 0\le\tau_j(S_j)-\tau_j(t_j)\le1\qquad(j\ge J).
\]
<!-- end introlemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The target relation and $\beta_jx_{j-1}^2\ge1/2$ give
\[
 \tau_j(t_j)=\frac{x_j}{\sqrt{\beta_j}}
 \le\sqrt2\,x_jx_{j-1}.
\]
The additional scaled time after the target is
\[
 \tau_j(S_j)-\tau_j(t_j)
 =2\sqrt{a_jh_{j-1}}W_{j+1}
 =6\sqrt{a_j}\,x_{j+1}x_j\sqrt{\frac{h_{j-1}}{h_j}}.
\]
For $j>J$, the logarithm of the square-root factor is
\[
 \frac12\log\frac{h_{j-1}}{h_j}
 =\frac{x_{j-1}}{2(j-1)^7}-\frac{x_{j-1}}{2j^5}
 \le-\frac{x_{j-1}}{4j^5}
\]
for sufficiently large $J$. Its exponential dominates the factor
$x_{j+1}x_j$, so the additional scaled time is at most $1$.
For $j=J$, \eqref{intro:eq:seed-scales} gives instead
$(D_0/2)\log x_{J-1}-x_{J-1}/(2J^5)$, with the same conclusion
for sufficiently large $x_{J-1}$. Therefore
\[
 \tau_j(S_j)\le\sqrt2\,x_jx_{j-1}+1
 \le2x_jx_{j-1}=\Theta_j.
\]
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- introlemma-2: body_md -->
\label{intro:lem:clock-parent}
If $a_j\ge1/2$, as in \eqref{intro:eq:activation-ranges}, then
\[
 \Theta_j\le\tau_j(S_{j-1}).
\]
<!-- end introlemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Since $a_j\ge1/2$, the definitions give
\[
 \frac{\varepsilon_j\Theta_j}{a_j}
 =\frac{2x_jx_{j-1}}{\sqrt{a_jh_{j-1}}}
  \le\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}W_j<2W_j=S_{j-1}-t_{j-1}.
\]
Multiplying by $a_j/\varepsilon_j$ gives
$\Theta_j<\tau_j(S_{j-1})$, which implies the stated bound.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
